t: Minimum Number of Coins for Fruits II
o: Same reward structure as the medium version (buying fruit i covers the next i fruits) but n up to 10^5, so the O(n²) DP is too slow. The DP transition f[i] = min over j in a growing suffix-window of (f[j] + prices[j]) is a sliding-window minimum, solvable with a monotonic deque in O(n).
k: f[i] = min cost to acquire fruits 1..i satisfies f[i] = min over j with 2j ≥ i−1 (1-indexed purchase j) of f[j−1] + prices[j].
The lower bound of the candidate window is non-decreasing, enabling a monotonic deque of increasing values.
Each index is pushed/popped once → linear time.

a.i: Work 0-indexed: buying index j costs prices[j] and covers through 2j+1 fruits, so f[i] draws candidates j from ⌈i/2⌉−1 to i−1. Keep a deque of candidate indices with strictly increasing g[j] = f[j]+prices[j]; the front is the window minimum. As i grows, evict front indices below the window and push newly eligible ones.
s: For i = 1..n: pop front while index < lo(i); f[i] = g(front).
Push index i−1 (its g uses freshly computed f[i−1]) after popping larger-or-equal tails.

c.python:
from collections import deque
from typing import List
class Solution:
    def minimumCoins(self, prices: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(prices)
        f = [0] * (n + 1)
        dq = deque([0])
        g = lambda j: f[j] + prices[j]
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            lo = max(0, (i + 1) // 2 - 1)
            while dq[0] < lo:
                dq.popleft()
            f[i] = g(dq[0])
            c = i - 1
            while dq and g(dq[-1]) >= g(c):
                dq.pop()
            dq.append(c)
        return f[n]

a.t: O(n) — amortized O(1) deque operations per index

a.i: Alternative structure: a min-segment-tree indexed by candidate j storing g[j]; each f[i] queries the range [lo(i), i−1] and then inserts g[i−1]. Slightly heavier but generalizes to arbitrary window updates.
s: Build a min segment tree of size n with +∞ defaults.
For each i: query min over [lo(i), i−1] → f[i]; point-update position i−1 with f[i−1]+prices[i−1].
a.t: O(n log n) — log-factor range-min queries

w: Derive the window bounds carefully (buying 0-indexed j covers fruits 0..2j, so f[i]'s candidates satisfy 2j+1 ≥ i). The deque is the intended optimal solution; the segment tree is a robust fallback if window logic feels error-prone. Watch the strict/non-strict comparison in the deque tail pop.
